chapter: First big band, his father, arriving in Kansas City
title: His 1937 marriage and his wife's reaction to his tips
summary: He married late in 1937; his wife did not understand a musician's life until he emptied a pocketful of tips, about $65-70, on the table.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Some I knew and some I didn't know. A lot of them I didn't know, you know, just -- you know how you just messing with people, you know. And so I went on home that night and I hadn't been married very long and the girl I was married to, she was quite -- I thought, unreasonable-like, you know what I mean. She didn't understand the musician's life, no way. She thought --
Well, were you married when you -- when you saw Billy Hadnot, you weren't married then?

It was late '37. And she didn't understand musician's life, you know, because she just didn't understand it. So when I came home that night -- she would have felt better if I had had a regular working job, if I

wasn't making but $12 a week or $15 a week. But she'd say, "I know he's working on the railroad," or whatever. You know what I mean, something like that. But anyway, I came home and I started pulling out these $1 bills and every once in a while, I'd see a five and it would shake me up, you know.
I kept pulling. I didn't realize -- she looked at me, she says, "What have you done?" She thought I'd robbed somebody or something.
Anyway, this was the first time she ever made sense to me. She said, "You mean you made this playing tonight?" I said, "Yeah." I didn't tell her about the check.

"Yeah, that's what I made." She said, "Listen, let me tell you something. You can go out and have all the fun you want. Go on out, if you want to go out and enjoy yourself." I said, "That's just what I'm going to do."
How much did you make altogether that night? Do you remember?

I'll tell you the truth. I think I made about -- must have been about 65 or $70. Just in tips, you know what I mean, and oh, I'll tell you. So that was so great. Well, you know, quite natural, I'm calling Mr. Bales every day,
